title: Nonlocal Orbital-Angular-Momentum Dichroism of Vortex Light in Strained Crystals
abstract: Vortex light carries orbital angular momentum (OAM) in its transverse phase, unlike spin, which is encoded in polarization. We show that this phase cannot produce OAM dichroism in any continuously translation-invariant system, even when optical nonlocality and multipole light--matter coupling are included. Nonuniform strain in a two-dimensional Dirac material bypasses this no-go condition by supplying transverse momentum transfer through a long-wavelength pseudo-gauge field, so that the OAM dichroism factorizes into a nonlocal elasto-optic tensor and the overlap of the vortex transverse phase current with the strain field. For a micron-scale Gaussian bubble, the resonant OAM-odd conductivity reaches \(\sim10^{-3}e^2/\hbar\), within reach of differential optical measurements.
summary: This theoretical paper demonstrates how nonuniform strain can induce Orbital-Angular-Momentum (OAM) dichroism in vortex light propagating through 2D Dirac materials. By breaking translational symmetry, the authors bypass a fundamental no-go theorem, showing that the measurable OAMD is governed by a factorable product of an elasto-optic tensor and the geometric overlap of the strain field with the vortex phase current.
main_problem: The study investigates the generation of Orbital-Angular-Momentum (OAM) dichroism ($\Delta\sigma_{OAM}$) for vortex light propagating through condensed matter systems.
main_result: OAMD requires broken continuous translational symmetry, which is achieved by applying nonuniform strain in a 2D Dirac material. The resulting OAMD factorizes into an elasto-optic tensor and the geometric overlap of the vortex phase current with the strain field.
method: The analysis uses a theoretical framework involving nonlocal optical response functions calculated via Wigner variables, expanding the conductivity kernel in terms of strain-induced pseudo-gauge fields.
model_or_system: The model employs a two-dimensional Dirac material Hamiltonian subjected to weak, nonuniform strain (e.g., a Gaussian bubble). The analysis considers both interband and intraband contributions to the optical response tensor.
key_observables: OAM dichroism contrast ($\Delta\sigma_{OAM}$), which is proportional to $	ext{Re}\left[ \mathbf{B}^{(\ell)}_{ab} \Lambda_{ab}^s(\omega) ight]$.
important_parameters: Nonuniform strain magnitude, vortex topological charge ($\ell$), and the tilt parameter ($\alpha$) in the Dirac Hamiltonian.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a weak, long-wavelength strain texture and relies on approximations such as expanding kernels to first order in external wave vector Q and assuming specific doping regimes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the geometric overlap tensor $B^{(\ell)}_{ab}$ dependence on displacement and beam waist, and show material coefficients entering the OAM-odd response, highlighting resonant enhancement.
paper_structure: The paper establishes a no-go theorem for translationally invariant systems, then introduces strain to bypass this. It develops the nonlocal conductivity tensor by expanding in strain, factorizing the result into geometric overlap and an elasto-optic tensor derived from solving the Boltzmann equation for both interband and intraband terms.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete mechanism—strain engineering—to generate a measurable optical signature (OAM dichroism) that is fundamentally forbidden in simpler, translationally invariant quantum systems. This bridges topological light properties with solid-state material response.

The sur- face represents a Gaussian strain bubble, with colour indicat- ing the deformation amplitude. The vortex core is displaced from the bubble center by the in-plane vector d. The circular arrows denote the vortex transverse phase current J (ℓ). This relative displacement breaks the common circular symmetry of the optical and strain profiles, enabling OAM-sensitive cou- pling through optical nonlocality.
